We need to determine if we can split an array into individual elements (n subarrays each of length one) through a series of splits, where each split must satisfy: when we split an existing array (contiguous segment of original array) into two contiguous subarrays, each resulting subarray must either have length 1, or have sum >= m.

Goal: Starting from the whole array, we can recursively split any subarray of length >=2 into two contiguous parts, as long as each part satisfies the condition (length==1 or sum >= m). Continue until all subarrays are length 1.

We need to return True if possible.

Observations: Since final subarrays are length 1, each element is alone, and length 1 satisfies condition automatically (since one of the conditions: length is one). So we just need to ensure we can split all the way down such that each split produces parts that either are singletons or have sufficient sum.

This is reminiscent of checking if we can partition array by successive splits where each internal node (segment that gets split) must have the property that both children satisfy either being leaf (size 1) or sum >= m. Equivalent to building a binary tree over the array (contiguous segmentation) where each internal node corresponds to a segment that was split; leaves are singletons; internal node's two children must each either be leaf (size 1) or have sum >= m.

We need to know if there exists such a binary tree.

Simplify: The process is akin to being able to recursively split any segment [l, r] (length >=2) into [l, k] and [k+1, r] such that both parts either have length 1 or sum >= m. Then we recursively need to be able to split each part further (if length>1). So we can define a DP: can[l][r] = True if segment nums[l..r] can be completely split into singletons via allowed splits.

Base case: length 1 -> True (no split needed). For length >=2: we need to find a split point k (l <= k < r) such that:

- left segment [l, k] either length==1 or sum(l,k) >= m
- right segment [k+1, r] either length==1 or sum(k+1,r) >= m
- AND can[l][k] is True (i.e., left can be further split into singletons)
- AND can
